title: Assessment of the Seasonality of Depressive Symptoms in Adolescents
official: Assessment of the Seasonality of Depressive Symptoms in Adolescents Receiving Care for Mental Health Reasons in a Pediatric Setting-or the ECLIPSE Study-Using the SPAQ Questionnaire
summary: The seasonality of affective disorders-particularly depressive symptoms-is well-documented in adults, yet it remains under-researched in adolescents. Recent studies, however, suggest that young people aged 11 to 20 experience marked seasonal fluctuations in mood. In both hospital pediatric settings and the ECLIPSE program, many adolescents are admitted due to depressive symptoms or suicidal crises; however, the role of seasonality in these cases remains largely unexplored. ECLIPSE (a Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Liaison and Emergency Consultation Team) is a service at the Rouen University Hospital dedicated to providing emergency and post-emergency care for children and adolescents experiencing psychological distress. It is designed for minors aged 3 to 16 whose psychological state requires prompt intervention, but not hospitalization. Clinical observation suggests that, for some patients, depressive manifestations follow an annual cycle. Identifying such seasonal patterns could help improve our understanding of vulnerability factors and enable the adaptation of prevention and care strategies. The Seasonal Pattern Assessment Questionnaire (SPAQ) (Reynaud et al., 2022)-used in adults (\>18 years old) to screen for seasonal affective disorder via a Global Seasonality Score (GSS)-is a simple, self-administered tool that can easily be used with adolescents. Its application in this context would allow for the assessment of the seasonality of depressive symptoms within this hospitalized population.

interventions.name: Measuring the intensity of the seasonality of depressive symptoms in adolescents

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 11-17 years.
* Hospitalization in a pediatric ward (or post-emergency pediatric psychiatric care within the ECLIPSE unit) for depressive symptoms/suicidal crisis linked to a depressive state (DSM-5 criteria).
* Proficiency in French and the ability to self-complete the SPAQ questionnaire following clinical stabilization.
* Provision of information to the minor and no objection from those holding parental authority (in accordance with local procedures).
* First inclusion only (in the event of readmission, the initial episode is the one considered).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Conditions that interfere with the completion of a reliable self-report questionnaire: moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder (ASD) with significant communication impairments, an acute mental state (severe psychotic disorganization, acute intoxication/withdrawal, delirium), or severe physical pain.
* Absence of a current depressive state.
* Manic/hypomanic episode predominant at the time of data collection (depressive symptoms take priority for the purpose of assessing seasonality).
* Insufficient command of the French language or sensory impairments that prevent the assessment from being administered, even with assistance.
* SPAQ not completed (or major missing data, rendering the GSS uninterpretable).
* Patient refusal.
